question: Only you see the die. You are paid what you report, up to 5 francs, but a 6 pays nothing. What do you report?
answer: Few lied all the way. Reports of 5 came far above one in six, and 6s, which paid nothing, far less often, yet many who cheated stopped short of the top. Lying a little lets people keep both the money and their picture of themselves as honest. The paper called it lies in disguise.
move: Watch the small bends you allow yourself because they still feel honest.
ask: Where do I round in my own favour and still call it honest?

options.label: Exactly what I rolled
options.mirror: Like an estimated 39%: honest, though nobody could ever have known. Many people simply are.

options.label: A bit more than I rolled
options.mirror: Like many: they nudged the number up but stopped short of 5. A small lie still feels honest.

options.label: 5, the top pay
options.mirror: Like about 1 in 5. Nobody was harmed, the money was the lab's, and the rules invited it.

scene.why: We want the money and to stay honest in our own eyes, so we lie only a little.

reference: Fischbacher & Föllmi-Heusi, Lies in disguise: an experimental study on cheating, Journal of the European Economic Association 11 (2013): 525-547
